record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: For stochastic parabolic equations viewed as stochastic distributed parameter systems, can null controllability or approximate controllability be obtained with only one control rather than two, beyond the special cases already known?

evidence.quote: (3) Null/approximate controllability for stochastic parabolic equations with one control. One needs two controls to get the null/approximate controllability for stochastic parabolic equations (e.g., [45]). We believe that one control is enough. However, except for some special cases (e.g., [23, 26]), we have no idea on how to prove that.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic parabolic equation of the form
  dy - Δy dt = (a y + χ_{G_0} u) dt + (b y + v) dW(t)  in (0,T) × G,
  y = 0 on (0,T) × ∂G,
  y(0) = y_0 in G,
where G ⊂ ℝ^n is a bounded domain with smooth boundary, G_0 ⋐ G is a nonempty open subdomain, T > 0, W is a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion on a filtered probability space (Ω, ℱ, {ℱ_t}_{t≥0}, ℙ), a, b ∈ L^∞_ℱ((0,T) × G), y_0 ∈ L^2(Ω, ℱ_0; L^2(G)), and (u, v) is a pair of adapted controls with u ∈ L^2_ℱ(0,T; L^2(G_0)) (the "drift control") and v ∈ L^2_ℱ(0,T; L^2(G)) (the "diffusion control"). It is known that null controllability and approximate controllability for such equations hold with two controls (u, v).

Question: Determine, beyond known special cases, whether null controllability (respectively approximate controllability) can be achieved using only the single drift control u (taking v ≡ 0), or more generally with only one control rather than two, for general stochastic parabolic equations of this type. Provide a proof or a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem appears to remain open. Recent works (2023–2024) establish null controllability with one control only in special structured cases — e.g., cascade/coupled systems where one control acts on the first equation and propagates via coupling, fourth-order stochastic parabolic equations, and Stackelberg–Nash settings. No result is found establishing one-control null/approximate controllability for general scalar stochastic parabolic equations beyond such special cases.

status_evidence.title: Null Controllability for Cascade systems of Coupled Backward Stochastic Parabolic Equations with One Distributed Control
status_evidence.snippet: Null controllability of cascade systems of n coupled backward stochastic parabolic equations ... with a single distributed control applied to the first equation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress addresses one-control null controllability only for specific cascade/coupled systems, not the general case.

status_evidence.title: Null controllability for stochastic coupled systems of fourth order parabolic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Null controllability for stochastic coupled systems of fourth order parabolic equations.
status_evidence.claim: One-control results exist for special fourth-order coupled stochastic parabolic systems.

status_evidence.title: Stackelberg-Nash null controllability for stochastic parabolic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Stackelberg-Nash null controllability for stochastic parabolic equations.
status_evidence.claim: Special hierarchical-control setups have been treated, but the general one-control problem is not resolved.
